import sys, json, uuid, hashlib, datetime

# THE ONE WRITER OF THE WALL (curator, GH #888). Everything that enters the
# window of the model behind this hive passes through here first and becomes
# ledger rows: a turn of the running round (`in_curate`), the model's own final
# answer (`in_llm`, the tap), a durable system slot (`in_slots` from the
# collector, `in_pack` from the identity pusher), a section of the model's
# sidecar block (`in_section`: `marks`), a pin of another hive (`in_pin`:
# `pins`), a gap's find `./push` kept for the round it opens (`in_addendum`,
# GH #895), a push candidate of another hive or an app (`in_candidate`:
# `candidates`, GH #949). Nothing here builds a window or calls a model -- that
# is `./policy`, and `./writer` hands episodes on. The one thing that leaves
# without a ledger row is the `things` section of the model's block, handed on
# as `thing_seen` (GH #949).
#
# Every lane runs the same two steps against `./ledger`:
#   A  park the payload in `state` (key `pending:<id>`) and read, in ONE bundle,
#      what is already there -- the payload comes back in the same answer, so
#      nothing large rides in a context key;
#   B  write only what is new (blocks by hash, wall rows by
#      (session_id, turn_id, hash, nth), slots by path) and hand on.
# THE LEDGER IS THE TRUTH (GH #1225, A1). Every write of B is ONE step that
# cannot double a row: a block is `insert` with `if_absent {hash}`, a wall row
# `insert` with `if_absent {session_id, turn_id, hash, nth}`, a slot `insert`
# with `replace` on its path under the unique index `slots_path` (K-4: read-
# before-write left 21 copies of one path in a live ledger). Step A's read only
# saves writes. The RAM below is no record of what was written -- a B answers
# `./policy`, never this cell, so a refused B left the RAM saying "written" and
# every later re-send of the round skipped the person's row. It only guards
# the writes IN FLIGHT: each A carries this child's id and the number of Bs it
# had sent (`epoch`); the ledger answers in order, so a B sent before the A is
# in A's read, and only a B sent after it -- or by another child -- is not.

# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. Every ledger read asks the store
# first (`round_where`, GH #932), so a hidden row never comes back at all; the
# Python gate stays as the second line behind it.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))

def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()

# prefix may carry its own time, every other channel gets the ingest clock.
# The guard is the INSTANCE, not the channel: at the HTTP door (and on the
# peer path) the caller names the channel, so on an instance with the prefix
# set any such caller can backdate a memory by picking a matching name.
# Bridged channels (telegram, phone) never match unless the prefix collides
# with their names. Set it only on a lab instance.
REPLAY_PREFIX = str(P.get("replay_channel_prefix", "") or "").strip()

# `pending_swept` mark. Parked rows of a message whose answer never came back
# (a child killed between A and B, a refused step) otherwise stay for ever.

except ValueError:

def replay_time():
    """The turn's own time, in the wall's form, when this round may carry one;
    None otherwise (switch off, a channel outside the prefix, no time, or a
    time that is not ISO 8601 -- an unreadable time is the ingest clock, never
    a guess). A time without an offset is UTC."""
    if not REPLAY_PREFIX or not str(ctx.get("channel") or "").startswith(REPLAY_PREFIX):
        return None
    raw = ctx.get("happened_at")
    if raw is None or (isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip()):
        return None
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(str(raw).strip().replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        # Said, never swallowed (GH #1225): a replay whose turns all fall back
        # to the ingest clock measures a different system. The value is not
        # echoed -- a header a caller names can carry anything.
        sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: happened_at on replay channel is no ISO 8601"
                         " time -- the turn keeps the ingest clock\n")
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return t.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)


def next_seq(n):
    """`n` fresh wall sequence numbers: microseconds since the epoch, strictly
    above anything this child minted before. The store has no autoincrement, and
    this cell is the wall's only writer, so a clock reading made strictly
    monotonic here is the order of arrival. Above the ledger's own maximum
    too (GH #1225, A10): step A of every wall lane reads `max(seq)` (`a-seq`),
    so neither a new child nor a clock set back mints a number below a row
    that stands."""
    base = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000000)
    base = max(base, _MEM["seq"] + 1)
    _MEM["seq"] = base + n - 1
    return [base + i for i in range(n)]


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=""):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def lstore(ops, phase, reply=ME, call="", reason=""):
    """One message to `./ledger`. Every key the edge reads is always present
    (a failed CEL modifier skips the edge)."""
    return {"header": {"route": "lstore", "phase": phase, "reply_cell": reply,
                       "cur_call": call, "cur_reason": reason},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in ops]}


def legs(body):
    """The answer of a store message by tool_call id: payload, error code and
    rows affected -- for a bundle (`results[]`) and for a single op alike."""
    out = {}
    msgs = body.get("messages") or []
    results = body.get("results")
    for m in msgs:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None

def tool_failure(el):
    """`(failed, code)` of one `tool_result` turn (GH #925). A tool says it
    failed on the turn (`finish_reason` "error", an `error_code`) or in its
    text, in the forms the shipped tools answer in: `{"error": "<code>", ...}`
    (the curator's history tools), `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", ...}}` (the
    file tools), a bare `ok: false` or an `error_code`. A refusal a tool says
    only on its hop never reaches a round, and prose is no failure. Every
    place counts as a failure whatever it says; the code is the first of them
    in the narrow form of a code (`error_code`; "" when none is -- a sentence
    is no code, OR-BD-6, a file name is none, review m-5, nor a word with a
    digit or a `-`, review R2-I-2). An
    `error` string that says there is none (NO_ERROR) is no failure."""
    raw = str(el.get("error_code") or "").strip()
    failed = bool(raw) or str(el.get("finish_reason") or "") == "error"
    code = error_code(raw)
    try:
        body = json.loads(str(el.get("text") or ""))
    except ValueError:
        body = None
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        err = body.get("error")
        if isinstance(err, str) and err.strip() and err.strip().lower() not in NO_ERROR:
            failed, code = True, code or error_code(err)
        elif isinstance(err, dict) and err:
            failed, code = True, code or error_code(err.get("code"))
        if body.get("ok") is False:
            failed = True
        own = body.get("error_code")
        if isinstance(own, str) and own.strip():
            failed, code = True, code or error_code(own)
    return failed, code


def sidecar_sections(text):
    """The sections of an answer's ```sidecar block: the one JSON object
    between the fence line and the closing fence, its top-level keys the
    sections (the talky splitter's grammar, GH #605) -- or {} when there is
    none that reads. The legacy ```memory fence is the single section
    `memory` and names no other."""
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return {}
    block = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    head = block.find("\n")
    if head < 0 or not block.lower().startswith(FENCE):
        return {}
    inner = block[head + 1:]
    if inner.endswith("```"):
        inner = inner[:-3]
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(inner.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {}

    the model rewriting a standing instruction (the core's advice to rewrite

    in a block."""
    out = []
    for m in messages:

def leaves_of(tree, prefix=""):
    """The (path, text) leaves of a `system` tree and its `$replace` roots, read
    the way the `llm` cell reads them: an object with `text` is a leaf, `$`-keys
    are markers, anything that is not an object is nothing."""
    leaves, roots = [], []
    if not isinstance(tree, dict):
        return leaves, roots
    if tree.get("$replace") is True:
        roots.append(prefix)
    if "text" in tree and prefix:
        leaves.append((prefix, str(tree.get("text") or "")))
        return leaves, roots
    for k in sorted(tree):
        if k.startswith("$"):
            continue
        path = k if not prefix else prefix + "." + k
        lv, rt = leaves_of(tree[k], path)
        leaves += lv
        roots += rt
    return leaves, roots


def slot_element(path, text):

def session_bound(path):
    """Whether `path` is a slot of one session (SESSION_SLOTS, review I-4):
    the path itself or one below it."""
    return any(path == p or path.startswith(p + ".") for p in SESSION_SLOTS)


def session_leaves(system):
    """The leaves of a session's own slots in one `system` tree, as sorted
    `[path, text]` pairs -- what a call parks beside its turn (review I-4)."""
    return sorted([p, t] for p, t in leaves_of(system)[0] if session_bound(p))


def slot_ops(current, system, owner, stamp, pfx):
    """Blocks and slot writes for one incoming `system` tree.

    The collector wins at its own leaf paths: a pack leaf on a path the
    collector holds is not written. A `$replace` root drops this owner's rows
    below it that the tree no longer names -- never another owner's.
    A slot of one session (`session_bound`) is never written here, and a row
    under one that a ledger from before review I-4 still holds is deleted
    in the same bundle, whoever wrote it: no reader takes it any more.

    GH #1225 (K-4): step A decides WHETHER a slot is written, never HOW --
    every write is ONE `insert` with `replace` on the path, so a second
    message in flight that also read "missing" replaces instead of adding a
    copy (live: 21 copies of one path, `window_est` x21). A pack write
    replaces only pack rows (`{"path", "owner": "pack"}`): when a collector
    row landed after step A read, the insert hits the unique index
    `slots_path`, the replace rolls back, and the collector keeps the path --
    `unique_violation` on a pack leg is that verdict, not a fault. A path
    the ledger holds more than once (a ledger from before the index) is
    always written: the replace takes every copy along, and the next wake
    builds the index (the GH #954 way, nothing deleted by hand)."""
    leaves, roots = leaves_of(system)
    have, copies = {}, {}
    for r in current:
        p = str(r.get("path") or "")
        have[p] = r
        copies.setdefault(p, []).append(r)
    stale = sorted(p for p in have if session_bound(p))
    blocks, ops, named = [], [], set()
    for i, (path, text) in enumerate(leaves):
        if session_bound(path):
            continue
        el = slot_element(path, text)
        h = block_hash(el)
        blocks.append((el, h, "system"))
        named.add(path)
        held = copies.get(path) or []
        if owner == "pack" and any(str(r.get("owner") or "") == "collector" for r in held):
            continue
        if len(held) == 1 and str(held[0].get("hash") or "") == h \
                and str(held[0].get("owner") or "") == owner:
            continue
        if owner == "pack":
            ops.append(("%s-sp%d" % (pfx, i), dict(
                ins("slots", {"path": path, "hash": h, "owner": owner, "at": stamp}),
                replace={"path": path, "owner": "pack"})))
        else:
            ops.append(("%s-sw%d" % (pfx, i), dict(
                ins("slots", {"path": path, "hash": h, "owner": owner, "at": stamp}),
                replace={"path": path})))
    gone = []
    for root in roots:
        for path, row in have.items():
            if str(row.get("owner") or "") != owner or path in named or path in gone \
                    or path in stale:
                continue
            if root == "" or path == root or path.startswith(root + "."):
                gone.append(path)
    if gone:
        ops.append(("%s-sd" % pfx, {"operation": "delete", "table": "slots",
                    "where": {"path": {"in": sorted(gone)}, "owner": owner}}))
    if stale:
        ops.append(("%s-ss" % pfx, {"operation": "delete", "table": "slots",
                    "where": {"path": {"in": stale}}}))
    return blocks, ops


def block_ops(items, have, stamp, pfx):
    """Inserts for the blocks step A did not find, each hash once, each ONE
    step with `if_absent {hash}` (GH #1225, A1): a block written in flight by
    another message stays as it stands, and a block whose write failed is
    written by the next message that names it -- no RAM says "written"."""
    ops, done = [], set(have)
    for i, (el, h, kind) in enumerate(items):
        if h in done:
            continue
        done.add(h)
        body = canonical(el)
        op = ins("blocks", {
            "hash": h, "kind": kind, "chars": len(str(el.get("text") or "")),
            "body": body, "first_seen": stamp})
        op["if_absent"] = {"hash": h}
        ops.append(("%s-b%d" % (pfx, i), op))
    return ops

    if not key.startswith("pending:"):

def sweep_cut():
    return (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
            - datetime.timedelta(seconds=PENDING_SWEEP_S)).strftime(FMT)


def sweep_candidates(keys):
    """The parked keys of this cell whose time this child does not know or
    knows to be past `pending_sweep_s`: their values are read once more
    (`s-rows`, off the call's path) and the old ones dropped. A key this child
    parked itself and saw young is not read again until it is old."""
    cut = sweep_cut()
    for k in [k for k, t in _MEM["parked"].items() if t < cut]:
        del _MEM["parked"][k]
    return sorted({k for k in keys if own_pending(k) and k not in _MEM["parked"]})


def epoch_now():
    """What an A carries: this child and the number of Bs it has sent."""
    return [_MEM["child"], _MEM["epoch"]]


def in_flight(epoch):
    """The test of a RAM entry for the A that carried `epoch`: True when the
    B that wrote it left after that A (so A's read could not see it), or when
    another child sent the A (every B of this child left after it)."""
    child, sent = (epoch if isinstance(epoch, list) and len(epoch) == 2 else ["", 0])
    if child != _MEM["child"]:
        return lambda e: True
    try:
        sent = int(sent)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        sent = 0
    wall = _MEM["wall"]
    for k in [k for k, v in wall.items() if v[-1] <= sent]:
        del wall[k]
    return lambda e: e > sent

def section_marks(section, payload):
    """The `marks` rows `(kind, value)` one section leaves, in the order they
    are written: in a `window` section the releases before the pins, so a pin
    of the same id in the same block is the later word (review focus 2)."""
    payload = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
    if section == "memory":
        # OR-KY-71: the mark carries the topic's name beside its movement, as
        # canonical JSON like the `gap` mark -- a reader of the ledger (the
        # handover, the push) has to know WHICH topic is open, not only that
        # one moved. `name` is "" when the section names none.
        topic = payload.get("topic") if isinstance(payload.get("topic"), dict) else {}
        move = str(topic.get("movement") or "").strip().lower()
        if move not in TOPIC_MOVES:
            return []
        name = str(topic.get("name") or "").strip()
        value = {"movement": move, "name": name}
        # GH #1225 (OR-KF-8): a topic files under its source like a fact, in
        # the mark's value; a token outside the vocabulary is not written.
        form = source_form(topic.get("source"))
        if form is not None:
            value["source"] = source_token(form)
        return [("topic", canonical(value))]
    if section == "window":
        out = []
        for kind in ("release", "pin"):
            items = payload.get(kind)
            items = items if isinstance(items, list) else ([items] if items else [])
            for item in items:
                mid = norm_id(item)
                if mid:
                    out.append((kind, mid))
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: window %s %r is not a block id"
                                     " -- ignored\n" % (kind, item))
        return out
    return []

QUOTE_FOLD.update({ord(c): '"' for c in "“”„‟″«»"})
QUOTE_FOLD.update({ord(c): "-" for c in "–—―‐‑"})
# Under this many words a quote counts only as a whole turn: "yes" or "I do"
# stand in almost every source and prove nothing.
QUOTE_MIN_WORDS = 3


def quote_form(text):
    """The normal form both sides of the check are compared in: NFC, the
    typography folded, casefolded, any whitespace one space, punctuation at
    the edges stripped. Nothing else -- the words stay the words."""
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", str(text)).translate(QUOTE_FOLD).casefold()
    s = " ".join(s.split())
    i, j = 0, len(s)
    while i < j and (s[i].isspace() or unicodedata.category(s[i]).startswith("P")):
        i += 1
    while j > i and (s[j - 1].isspace() or unicodedata.category(s[j - 1]).startswith("P")):
        j -= 1
    return s[i:j]


def quote_in(quote, sources):
    """Whether `quote` stands word for word in one of `sources`: its normal
    form inside the source's, at word boundaries -- a quote of fewer than
    QUOTE_MIN_WORDS words only as a whole source."""
    q = quote_form(quote)
    if not q:
        return False
    whole_only = len(q.split()) < QUOTE_MIN_WORDS
    for src in sources:
        s = quote_form(src)
        if whole_only:
            if q == s:
                return True
            continue
        at = s.find(q)
        while at >= 0:
            end = at + len(q)
            if (at == 0 or not s[at - 1].isalnum()) and (end == len(s) or not s[end].isalnum()):
                return True
            at = s.find(q, at + 1)
    return False


def frame_id(text, prefix):
    """The id of an `[app <id>]` / `[timer <id>]` frame, "" when it has none
    in the form of a name."""
    rest = str(text)[len(prefix):]
    if "]" not in rest:
        return ""
    tok = rest.split("]", 1)[0].strip()
    ok = tok and len(tok) <= 64 and all(c in CODE_CHARS for c in tok)
    return tok if ok else ""


def source_form(token):
    """An item's source read: ("person", "") | ("peer", <ref>) |
    ("agent", <name>), or None for a token outside the vocabulary."""
    t = token.strip().casefold() if isinstance(token, str) else ""
    if t == "person":
        return ("person", "")
    # A bare reference is a peer, the form of before (the `[peer <ref> ...]`
    # line a model copies).
    ref = t[5:] if t.startswith("peer:") else t
    if len(ref) in (8, 12) and all(c in PEER_REF_CHARS for c in ref):
        return ("peer", ref)
    if t.startswith("peer:"):
        return None
    if t.startswith("agent:"):
        name = t[6:]
        if name in AGENT_NAMES:
            return ("agent", name)
        for kind in ("app:", "timer:"):
            tail = name[len(kind):]
            if name.startswith(kind) and tail and len(tail) <= 64 \
                    and all(c in CODE_CHARS for c in tail):
                return ("agent", name)
    return None


def source_token(form):
    """The one spelling of a source read by `source_form`."""
    kind, name = form
    return kind if kind == "person" else "%s:%s" % (kind, name)


def source_pools(bodies, answer):
    """The words of every source a `source` rule may name: `(group, element)`
    pairs read off the wall, and the answer text the splitter stamped."""
    pools = {"person": [], "peer": {}, "agent": {"self": [answer] if answer else []}}
    for group, el in bodies:
        text = str(el.get("text") or "")
        if group == "user":
            pools["person"].append(text)
        elif group == "peer":
            ref = str(el.get("speaker_ref") or "")
            if ref:
                pools["peer"].setdefault(ref, []).append(text)
        elif group in AGENT_OF_KIND:
            pools["agent"].setdefault(AGENT_OF_KIND[group], []).append(text)
        elif group in ("app", "timer"):
            fid = frame_id(text, APP_PREFIX if group == "app" else TIMER_PREFIX)
            if fid:
                pools["agent"].setdefault(group + ":" + fid, []).append(text)
        elif group == "self":
            pools["agent"]["self"].append(stripped_text(text))
    return pools


def item_sources(item, pools):
    """The words the source an item names said, and "" -- or None and the
    reason that source cannot be checked."""
    token = item.get("source") if isinstance(item, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token.strip():
        return None, "source_missing"
    form = source_form(token)
    if form is None:
        return None, "source_unknown"
    kind, name = form
    if kind == "person":
        return pools["person"], ""
    if kind == "peer":
        if name not in pools["peer"]:
            return None, "source_unknown"
        return pools["peer"][name], ""
    return pools["agent"].get(name) or [], ""


def reject_value(section, field, reason, token, index=None):
    """The value of a `verify_reject` mark: where and why, and the source
    only in its form -- never the item's words."""
    form = source_form(token)
    v = {"section": section, "field": field, "reason": reason,
         "source": source_token(form) if form else ""}
    if index is not None:
        v["item"] = index
    return canonical(v)


def episode_index(episode, session):
    """The index of the person's episode `episode` names, when it is an id of
    THIS round of `session` (`episode_turn_id`); None otherwise."""
    _, sep, tail = str(episode or "").rpartition("-")
    if not sep or not tail.isdigit():
        return None
    n = int(tail)
    return n if episode_turn_id(session, ROW_AUDIENCE, n) == episode else None


def source_src(check, turn_rows, episode_rows):
    """`[hash, group, of_turn]` of every row a `source` rule reads: the turn's
    rows by kind (a final answer is `self`), the episode's person rows and the
    final answers after them."""
    idx = check.get("episode_idx")
    out = set()
    for r in turn_rows:
        h, k = str(r.get("hash") or ""), str(r.get("kind") or "")
        if not h:
            continue
        if k == "assistant":
            if int(r.get("final") or 0):
                out.add((h, "self", 1))
        elif k in SOURCE_KINDS or k == "recall":
            out.add((h, k, 1))
    for r in episode_rows:
        h, k = str(r.get("hash") or ""), str(r.get("kind") or "")
        try:
            at = int(r.get("episode_idx"))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        if not h or idx is None:
            continue
        if at == idx and k in ("user", "peer"):
            out.add((h, k, 0))
        elif at > idx and k == "assistant" and int(r.get("final") or 0):
            out.add((h, "self", 0))
    return sorted(out)


def verify_rule(raw):
    """The rule the splitter stamped, read: `{"fields": [(field, source)],
    "mode", "items", "typos"}`, the fields in the stamp's order (canonical,
    keys sorted) -- or None when it names no field with a known source."""
    try:
        rule = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else raw
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(rule, dict):
        return None
    fields = [(str(k), v) for k, v in rule.items()
              if k not in VERIFY_KEYS and v in VERIFY_SOURCES]
    if not fields:
        return None
    mode = rule.get("mode") if rule.get("mode") in VERIFY_MODES else "drop"
    items = rule.get("items") if isinstance(rule.get("items"), str) else ""
    # A typo is said, never swallowed: the operator reads stderr, not the
    # fallback.
    typos = []
    if "mode" in rule and rule["mode"] not in VERIFY_MODES:
        typos.append("mode %s is neither drop nor mark -- checked as drop"
                     % json.dumps(rule["mode"])[:40])
    if "items" in rule and not isinstance(rule["items"], str):
        typos.append("items %s is no array name -- the first array is checked"
                     % json.dumps(rule["items"])[:40])
    return {"fields": fields, "mode": mode, "items": items, "typos": typos}


def verify_of(section, body):
    """What step A parks for a section the splitter stamped, or None for one
    it did not (the section then goes the way it always went). `kinds` are
    the wall rows the rule reads: `user`/`peer` for `turn`, `recall` beside
    them for `turn+recall`, none for `answer` alone -- and none for a rule
    that names no known source, which checks nothing."""
    raw = hop.get("sidecar_verify")
    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
        return None
    if section in VERIFY_NEVER or (section == "memory" and section not in PASS_SECTIONS):
        sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: section %r is not checked here -- its"
                         " sidecar_verify is ignored\n" % section)
        return None
    rule = verify_rule(raw)
    if rule is None:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: section %r carries a sidecar_verify that names"
                         " no known source -- handed on unchecked\n" % section)
    sources = {s for _, s in (rule or {}).get("fields", [])}
    kinds = []
    if sources & {"turn", "turn+recall"}:
        kinds = ["user", "peer"] + (["recall"] if "turn+recall" in sources else [])
    out = {"rule": raw, "section": section, "kinds": kinds,
           "head": {k: v for k, v in hop.items() if k not in ("route", "sidecar_verify")},
           "body": {k: v for k, v in body.items() if k != "verify_answer"},
           "answer": str(body.get("verify_answer") or ""),
           "session": str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "default"),
           "turn": str(hop.get("turn_id") or ctx.get("turn_id") or ""),
           "episode": str(ctx.get("episode_turn_id") or hop.get("episode_turn_id") or "")}
    if "source" in sources:
        # GH #1225: every row a source may name, of the turn and of its episode.
        out["kinds"] = kinds + [k for k in SOURCE_KINDS if k not in kinds]
        out["by_source"] = 1
        idx = episode_index(out["episode"], out["session"])
        if idx is not None:
            out["episode_idx"] = idx
    return out


def verify_items(rule, payload, sources, pools=None, read_failed=False):
    """The section's payload after the check, and `(field, reason)` -- its
    first failed field -- per item that failed. The array is the rule's
    `items`, else the first list in the payload; without one there is nothing
    to check. A passing item gains `verified` (its fields, in the rule's
    order); a failing one is dropped, or under `mode` "mark" kept with
    `verified` and `failed`. A model's own `verified`/`failed` never stays: a
    claim of proof is no proof."""
    key = rule["items"] or next((k for k, v in payload.items() if isinstance(v, list)), "")
    items = payload.get(key) if key else None
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return payload, []
    kept, refused = [], []
    for index, item in enumerate(items):
        passed, failed = [], []
        for field, source in rule["fields"]:
            value = item.get(field) if isinstance(item, dict) else None
            words = sources.get(source) or []
            if read_failed and source in ("source", "turn", "turn+recall"):
                # GH #1225 (A3): rows that could not be read prove nothing and
                # refute nothing -- `store_error`, never `quote_not_in_source`.
                failed.append((field, "store_error"))
                continue
            if source == "source":
                # GH #1225: the rows of the source the item names.
                words, why = item_sources(item, pools or source_pools([], ""))
                if why:
                    failed.append((field, why))
                    continue
            if not isinstance(value, str) or not quote_form(value):
                failed.append((field, "quote_missing"))
            elif not quote_in(value, words):
                failed.append((field, "quote_not_in_source"))
            else:
                passed.append(field)
        bare = ({k: v for k, v in item.items() if k not in ("verified", "failed")}
                if isinstance(item, dict) else None)
        if not failed:
            kept.append(dict(bare, verified=passed))
            continue
        field0 = failed[0][0]
        by_source = any(f == field0 and s == "source" for f, s in rule["fields"])
        token = item.get("source") if isinstance(item, dict) else None
        refused.append(failed[0] + ((index, token) if by_source else ()))
        if rule["mode"] == "mark" and bare is not None:
            kept.append(dict(bare, verified=passed,
                             failed=[{"field": f, "reason": r} for f, r in failed]))
    out = dict(payload)
    out[key] = kept
    return out, refused


def verified_section(check, turns, recalls, pools=None, read_failed=False):
    """The checked section on `sidecar` -- the splitter's hop and body without
    the rule and the answer text -- and one `reject` per item that failed,
    naming section, field and reason and never the item's words: the refusal
    is a count for the parent's drain, not a copy of the claim. A section
    whose items all failed still leaves, with an empty array, so a reader
    tells "annotated, nothing proven" from "not annotated". Beside it the
    `verify_reject` marks `(kind, value)` of the refusals of a `source` rule
    (GH #1225, R-KF-5)."""
    rule = verify_rule(check.get("rule"))
    body = dict(check.get("body") or {})
    payload = body.get("payload") if isinstance(body.get("payload"), dict) else {}
    answer = str(check.get("answer") or "")
    sources = {"turn": turns, "turn+recall": turns + recalls,
               "answer": [answer] if answer else []}
    if rule:
        for typo in rule["typos"]:
            sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: section %r sidecar_verify %s\n"
                             % (str(check.get("section") or ""), typo))
        key = rule["items"] or next((k for k, v in payload.items() if isinstance(v, list)), "")
        if not isinstance(payload.get(key) if key else None, list):
            sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: section %r has no array items %r to check"
                             " -- handed on unchecked\n" % (str(check.get("section") or ""), key))
    payload, refused = (verify_items(rule, payload, sources, pools, read_failed) if rule
                        else (payload, []))
    head = dict(check.get("head") or {})
    head["route"] = "sidecar"
    head["section"] = str(check.get("section") or "")
    body["payload"] = payload
    out = [dict(body, header=head)]
    marks = [("verify_reject", reject_value(head["section"], r[0], r[1], r[3], r[2]))
             for r in refused if len(r) > 2]
    for field, reason in [r[:2] for r in refused]:
        out.append({"header": {"route": "reject", "reject_reason": reason,
                               "section": head["section"], "field": field,
                               "session_id": str(check.get("session") or ""),
                               "turn_id": str(check.get("turn") or ""),
                               "episode_turn_id": str(check.get("episode") or "")},
                    "messages": []})
    return out, marks


def source_ok(source):
    """A pinning hive's name: one path segment of `pinned.<source>.<id>`,
    never the model's own."""
    return bool(source) and source != MODEL_SOURCE and len(source) <= 64 \
        and all(c in PIN_SOURCE_CHARS for c in source)


def replace_of(body):
    """`replace_sources` of an `in_pin` body as (sources, reason). Absent is
    ([], ""); anything malformed refuses the whole message (reason set): a
    replacement half understood would end the wrong pins or keep stale ones."""
    if "replace_sources" not in body:
        return [], ""
    raw = body.get("replace_sources")
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        return [], "replace_sources is not a list"
    if len(raw) > REPLACE_MAX_SOURCES:
        return [], "replace_sources names %d sources, over %d" % (len(raw), REPLACE_MAX_SOURCES)
    out = []
    for s in raw:
        if not isinstance(s, str) or not source_ok(s):
            return [], "replace_sources: %r is no pinning hive's name" % (s,)
        if s not in out:
            out.append(s)
    return out, ""


def pin_live(until, as_of):
    """Whether a `pins` row still stands at `as_of` (an aware datetime): no
    `until`, or one that does not read as a time, stands for ever -- the rule
    `./handover` `pin_valid` and `./policy` `pin_split` read it by."""
    u = str(until or "").strip()
    if not u:
        return True
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(u.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return True
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return t > as_of


def pin_round(p):
    """The round ONE pin of `in_pin` stands in (GH #972, R-NL-4), as
    `(round, "")`, `(None, reason)` for a pin that waits (`pin:held`), or
    `("", reason)` for one refused outright.

    The ceiling is the round on the message (`context.audience_set`), which
    the builder's edge of the app's pin lane stamps with the app's MEMBER
    round, after every edge of the app. A pin without its own `audience_set`
    takes the ceiling (the rule before #972). A pin that names one keeps it
    when it is (a) the round of the turn this message belongs to
    (`TURN_ROUND`, which no app can set) or (b) inside the ceiling (`cand_narrows`:
    a narrower round, or the ceiling itself). Anything else -- a group round
    claimed outside a turn of that group -- is not placed: it waits until the
    app pins it again in a turn of that round. Fail-closed: no ceiling, no pin."""
    if "audience_set" not in p or p.get("audience_set") is None:
        return AUDIENCE, ""
    aud = audience_of(p.get("audience_set"))
    if aud is None:
        return "", "audience_set %r is no round" % (p.get("audience_set"),)
    if TURN_ROUND is not None and aud == TURN_ROUND:
        return aud, ""
    if cand_narrows(AUDIENCE, aud):
        return aud, ""
    if TURN_ROUND is None:
        return None, "round %s is wider than %s and no turn proves it" % (aud, AUDIENCE)
    return None, "round %s is wider than %s and not the round %s of this turn" % (
        aud, AUDIENCE, TURN_ROUND)


def pin_of(p, stamp):
    """One pin of `in_pin` as (element, row), or a reason it is refused."""
    if not isinstance(p, dict):
        return None, "a pin is an object"
    text = str(p.get("text") or "")
    source = str(p.get("source") or "")
    until = str(p.get("until") or "").strip()
    if not text.strip():
        return None, "a pin without text"
    size = len(json.dumps({"text": text}, ensure_ascii=False,
                          separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8"))
    if size > LEAF_MAX_BYTES:
        return None, "too_long: %d > %d bytes" % (size, LEAF_MAX_BYTES)
    if not source_ok(source):
        return None, "source %r is no pinning hive's name" % source
    if until:
        try:
            datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(until.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        except ValueError:
            return None, "until %r is no RFC 3339 time" % until
    el = {"type": "pin", "source": source, "text": text}
    return el, {"hash": block_hash(el), "source": source, "until": until, "at": stamp}


def cand_narrows(round_canon, cand_canon):
    """Whether a candidate's own audience stays inside the round it came in
    (GH #949), both canonical: every member it names is in the round, `*`
    only when the round holds `*`, and the empty set -- the audience of the
    round-less conversation, which a call without a round is shown -- only in
    an empty round. A round that holds `*` may name anyone."""
    r, c = set(json.loads(round_canon)), set(json.loads(cand_canon))
    if "*" in r:
        return True
    if "*" in c:
        return False
    if not c:
        return not r
    return c <= r


def candidate_of(c, source):
    """One entry of `in_candidate` (GH #949) as `(entry, "")`, or `(None,
    error_code)`: `audience_widened` for an audience the round does not hold,
    `invalid_input` for a field out of its bounds. The entry is the block
    element and the `candidates` row without `used_at`, `last_seq` and `at`,
    which step B sets. The round is fail-closed and checked before the other
    fields, so a widening is named as such whatever else is wrong."""
    if not isinstance(c, dict):
        return None, "invalid_input"
    cid, text = c.get("id"), c.get("text")
    if not isinstance(cid, str) or not cid.strip() or len(cid) > CAND_ID_MAX_CHARS:
        return None, "invalid_input"
    if c.get("audience_set") is None:
        aud = AUDIENCE
    else:
        aud = audience_of(c.get("audience_set"))
        if aud is None:
            return None, "invalid_input"
        if not cand_narrows(AUDIENCE, aud):
            return None, "audience_widened"
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        return None, "invalid_input"
    triggers = [] if c.get("triggers") is None else c.get("triggers")
    if not isinstance(triggers, list) or len(triggers) > CAND_TRIGGERS_MAX:
        return None, "invalid_input"
    for t in triggers:
        # A trigger without a letter or a digit (`?!`, `...`, a blank) would
        # stand in nearly every turn once the push tokenises it -- refused,
        # never stripped into something the sender did not write.
        if not isinstance(t, str) or len(t) > CAND_TRIGGER_MAX_CHARS \
                or not any(ch.isalnum() for ch in t):
            return None, "invalid_input"
    once = (not triggers) if c.get("once") is None else c.get("once")
    if not isinstance(once, bool):
        return None, "invalid_input"
    prio = CAND_PRIORITY_DEFAULT if c.get("priority") is None else c.get("priority")
    if isinstance(prio, bool) or not isinstance(prio, int) \
            or not 0 <= prio <= CAND_PRIORITY_MAX:
        return None, "invalid_input"
    until = "" if c.get("until") is None else c.get("until")
    if not isinstance(until, str):
        return None, "invalid_input"
    until = until.strip()
    if until:
        # The form of a pin's `until` (`pin_of`): RFC 3339, kept as given --
        # one in the past is kept too and never shown.
        try:
            datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(until.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        except ValueError:
            return None, "invalid_input"
    el = {"type": CAND_KIND, "source": source, "text": text}
    return {"element": el, "row": {
        "source": source, "cand_id": cid, "hash": block_hash(el),
        "triggers": canonical(triggers), "until": until, "once": 1 if once else 0,
        "priority": prio, "audience_set": aud}}, ""


def candidates_of(body):
    """An `in_candidate` body (GH #949) as `(source, kept, refused, withdraw,
    broken)`. `broken` names what is wrong when the body itself is -- a
    source that is no hive's name by the pin rule, `candidates` or `withdraw`
    not a list of at most CAND_MAX, an id of `withdraw` out of bounds, neither
    list at all -- and then nothing of it is kept. A repeated `id` is its
    LAST entry (a sender that corrects itself within one message); the earlier
    ones are neither kept nor refused."""
    source = body.get("source")
    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source_ok(source):
        return "", [], [], [], "source %r is no pushing hive's name" % (source,)
    if "candidates" not in body and "withdraw" not in body:
        return source, [], [], [], "neither candidates nor withdraw"
    raw = body.get("candidates", [])
    if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(raw) > CAND_MAX:
        return source, [], [], [], "candidates is no list of at most %d" % CAND_MAX
    gone = body.get("withdraw", [])
    if not isinstance(gone, list) or len(gone) > CAND_MAX \
            or any(not isinstance(g, str) or not g.strip() or len(g) > CAND_ID_MAX_CHARS
                   for g in gone):
        return source, [], [], [], "withdraw is no list of at most %d ids" % CAND_MAX
    last = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(raw):
        if isinstance(c, dict) and isinstance(c.get("id"), str):
            last[c["id"]] = i
    kept, refused = [], []
    for i, c in enumerate(raw):
        cid = c.get("id") if isinstance(c, dict) else None
        if isinstance(cid, str) and last.get(cid) != i:
            continue
        entry, code = candidate_of(c, source)
        if entry is None:
            refused.append({"id": cid[:CAND_ID_MAX_CHARS] if isinstance(cid, str) else "",
                            "error_code": code})
        else:
            kept.append(entry)
    return source, kept, refused, sorted(set(gone)), ""


def candidate_ack(source, stored, refused, code=""):
    """The receipt of one `in_candidate` (GH #949), or None when the sender
    did not ask for one with `hop.ack` "1": every curator behind a fan-out
    answers, and three receipts nobody drains are three dead letters per
    push. `stored` counts the candidates kept, `refused` names the others;
    `hop.error_code` is set when the whole body was refused."""
    if str(hop.get("ack") or "") != "1":
        return None

def as_int(value):
    try:
        return int(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def cand_change(old, row):
    """What a candidate pushed again does to its `candidates` row (GH #949):
    `(write, reset)`. `reset`: its text (the hash), `once` or its triggers
    moved, so it is a new candidate to the push and the push's own marks on
    it (`used_at`, `last_seq`) start over. `write`: anything moved, `until`,
    `priority` and the round included -- the latest door decides who it stands
    for, as with a pin. Nothing moved: no write, and the marks stay."""
    reset = (str(old.get("hash") or "") != row["hash"]
             or as_int(old.get("once")) != row["once"]
             or str(old.get("triggers") or "") != row["triggers"])
    write = reset or str(old.get("until") or "") != row["until"] \
        or as_int(old.get("priority")) != row["priority"] \
        or audience_of(old.get("audience_set")) != row["audience_set"]
    return write, reset


def thing_of(item):
    """One entry of a `things` section (GH #949) in its checked form, or None:
    `name` a non-empty string, `kind` and `note` strings, each stripped; an
    empty optional one is left out. An entry out of its form is left out whole
    and nothing but these three fields travels on. No field has a length of
    its own (OR-IG-11): the section's budget counts, in `things_of`."""
    if not isinstance(item, dict):
        return None
    name = item.get("name")
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
        return None
    out = {"name": name.strip()}
    for key in ("kind", "note"):
        v = item.get(key)
        if v is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(v, str):
            return None
        if v.strip():
            out[key] = v.strip()
    return out


def things_window():
    """The window (tokens) of the model the things came from: the smallest
    `input_soft` of the answer's hop, the context and `recall_input_soft`;
    None when none names one."""
    known = [int(float(v)) for v in (hop.get("input_soft"), ctx.get("input_soft"),
                                     ctx.get("recall_input_soft"))
             if budget_chars(v, 1.0) is not None]
    return min(known) if known else None


def _size(t):
    return sum(len(v) for v in t.values())


def things_of(payload, limit=None):
    """The entries of a `things` section (GH #949) and what was cut of them:
    `(items, cut)`. The list under `items` -- the splitter hands a section on
    only as an object and drops a bare list under a top-level key -- or the
    list itself, each by `thing_of`, a name once (case-folded), in the order
    written. Within `limit` characters (None: no limit) the entries go whole;
    the first one alone over it is clipped (note, then kind, then name) with a
    mark, and every entry after the last that fits is named in `cut`:
    `{"text": "...[dropped: ...]", "shown": k, "total": n}`, else None."""
    raw = payload.get("items") if isinstance(payload, dict) else payload
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        return [], None
    whole, seen = [], set()
    for item in raw:
        t = thing_of(item)
        if t is None:
            sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: a things entry out of its form -- left out\n")
            continue
        key = t["name"].casefold()
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            whole.append(t)
    total = sum(_size(t) for t in whole)
    if limit is None or total <= limit:
        return whole, None
    out, used, n = [], 0, 0
    while n < len(whole) and used + _size(whole[n]) <= limit:
        used += _size(whole[n])
        out.append(whole[n])
        n += 1
    if n < len(whole) and _size(whole[n]) > limit and used < limit:
        # Alone over the section's budget: it goes with its head and a mark,
        # never left out in silence (design section 2).
        t, excess = dict(whole[n]), used + _size(whole[n]) - limit
        for f in ("note", "kind", "name"):
            if excess > 0 and f in t:
                keep = max(0, len(t[f]) - excess)
                excess -= len(t[f]) - keep
                t[f] = clip(t[f], keep, THINGS_HINT)
        out.append(t)
        used, n = limit, n + 1
    rest = whole[n:]
    shown = used
    if not rest:
        return out, {"text": "", "shown": shown, "total": total}
    gone = sum(_size(t) for t in rest)
    text = "...[dropped: %d things (%d chars) over budget]" % (len(rest), gone)
    sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: things over the budget of the window -- %s\n" % text)
    return out, {"text": text, "shown": shown, "total": total}

def episode_turn_id(session, audience, index):
    """The id `./writer` gives an episode on `turn_write`, `<session>#<tag>-<index>`
    (GH #932) -- the same code, locked equal by gh941: the model call names the
    person's episode of its turn by it (GH #941), so whoever reads a section of
    the answer addresses that episode without building the id itself."""
    tag = hashlib.sha256(audience.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return "%s#%s-%d" % (session, tag, index)


def round_key(round_value):
    """The key the policy keeps a round's state under (GH #943): the first 12
    hex digits of the sha256 of the canonical round, `[]` for none -- the
    same formula as `round_key` in `./policy`, so a call reads the plan of
    its own round (OR-BC.W.1)."""
    return hashlib.sha256((audience_of(round_value) or "[]").encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


def stage_a(pid, stash, hashes, session="", turn="", cover=False, slots=False):
    """Step A: park the payload, read what is there -- one bundle."""
    # GH #1225 (A13): the time it was parked, for the sweep; (A1) the epoch.
    if stash.get("lane") != "in_pin" or "replace" in stash:
        stash = dict(stash, parked_at=now())
    wall_lane = stash.get("lane") in ("in_curate", "in_llm", "in_addendum")
    if wall_lane:
        # Every wall lane, with or without the turn's reads below: its B
        # writes wall rows and mints sequence numbers.
        stash["epoch"] = epoch_now()
    _MEM["parked"][pending_key(pid)] = stash.get("parked_at") or now()
    ops = [("a-put", ins("state", {"key": pending_key(pid), "value": canonical(stash)})),
           ("a-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": pending_key(pid)}))]
    if wall_lane:
        # GH #1225 (A10): the ledger's newest sequence number, one row over
        # the index `wall_seq`, in the same bundle.
        ops.append(("a-seq", sel("wall", ["seq"], None, [("seq", "desc")], 1)))
    if cover:
        # GH #1225 (A13): the parked keys, names only -- `sweep_candidates`.
        ops.append(("a-pend", sel("state", ["key"], {"key": {"gte": "pending:"}},
                                  [("key", "asc")], PEND_READ)))
    if slots:
        ops.append(("a-slots", sel("slots", ["path", "hash", "owner"])))
    if hashes:
        ops.append(("a-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash"], {"hash": {"in": sorted(set(hashes))}})))
    if session:
        # Dedupe by key, unfiltered: the round's own rows of this turn, read to
        # write nothing twice (a turn is one round's).
        ops.append(("a-wall", sel("wall", ["hash", "nth"],
                                  {"session_id": session, "turn_id": turn})))
        # The last turn index of THIS round of the session (OR-S3.K.1): counted
        # over every round, the index a writer stamps into `turn_id` told a
        # round how many turns it did not see. Exact audience, so a `*` row or
        # one of a wider round is not counted -- each round counts from 0.
        ops.append(("a-epi", sel("wall", ["episode_idx"],
                                 {"session_id": session, "audience_set": ROW_AUDIENCE,
                                  "episode_idx": {"is_null": False}},
                                 [("episode_idx", "desc")], 1)))
        # The person's latest episode of THIS round of the session (GH #941):
        # the model call names it, so every sidecar section of the answer can
        # address it. A call that writes no person row -- a tool round, a
        # consult's advice coming back under a turn id of its own -- answers
        # the person's words that row holds. Exact audience, like the index.
        ops.append(("a-said", sel("wall", ["episode_idx"],
                                  {"session_id": session, "audience_set": ROW_AUDIENCE,
                                   "kind": {"in": ["user", "peer"]},
                                   "episode_idx": {"is_null": False}},
                                  [("episode_idx", "desc")], 1)))
    if cover:
        read = with_round("a-cover", "summaries", ["covers_to_seq"], None,
                          [("covers_to_seq", "desc")], 1)
        if read:
            ops.append(read)
        # The plan of THIS call's round (GH #943, OR-BC.W.1): the policy keeps
        # one plan per round, and a window cut by another round's plan
        # showed what that round's rebuild decided.
        ops.append(("a-plan", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                  {"key": "window_plan:" + round_key(ROW_AUDIENCE)})))
    return lstore(ops, "a", ME, pid, stash.get("lane", ""))
